To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rex4p and Rnt1p influence ITS1 processing and 5.85 rRNA synthesis by interacting with the trans-acting factors Rrp5p, Dbr1p and Rrp2p.
Rex4p, RNase MRP and RNase III, and the debranched enzyme Dbr1 are all required to ensure the production of 5,8SS rRNA.
Rex4p and Rnt1p are required for ITS1 processing and that Dbr1p is required for ITS2 processing in yeast
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processing of the ITS regions of the yeast ribosomal RNA precursor.
the role of RNA processing in the production of ribosomes in the yeast Sacch. cerevisiae.
the identification of factors involved in 5.8rRNA biogenesis and with the characterization of their function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of ITS1 is a highly complex process involving several trans-acting factors.
Rrp5p, Rex4p and Rnt1p are all involved in the processing of ITS2 and that the processing of ITS1 is affected by the presence or the absence of Rrp5p.
Rex4p and Rnt1p are involved in ITS1 processing and that the debranching activity of Dbr1p is required for efficient ITS1 processing
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three RNA catabolism enzymes Rex4p (RNase II), Rnt1p (RNase III), and Dbr1 (debranching) have been implicated in the production of the two 5.8 S rRNA species in yeast.
the RNA catabolic machinery in yeast is intimately linked to the pre-rRNA processing machinery.
Rex4p, Dbr1p and Rnt1p are all involved in the production of 5,8SS rRNA.

the RNA catabolic machinery is involved in the production of 5,8SS rRNA and in the regulation of the relative amounts of 5. 8SS and 8SS rRNA in the cells.
